A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VPO research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic-bandit experiments, ARC-Challenge accuracy comparisons, and online TL;DR preference evaluations in Section 5.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds contextual-bandit experiments and iterative VPO evaluations on AlpacaEval 2.0 and MT-Bench.

M1.justification: The VPO objectives, Algorithms 1–2, reward calibration framework, and token-level formulation remain unchanged. The buffer explanation and new iterative benchmark setup document implementations and experimental procedures without revising the proposed VPO method.

E1.justification: v4 adds linear contextual bandits with varying contexts and 50 actions, extending beyond the original single-context, ten-action problem. It also adds UltraFeedback training and AlpacaEval 2.0 and MT-Bench evaluation, substantially broadening instruction-following and conversational coverage. ARC-Challenge and TL;DR remain.

E2.justification: New Table 1 introduces numerical comparisons with SPIN, DNO, and SPPO, alongside iterative DPO and additional reference models. Several baseline results are explicitly sourced from prior work rather than established as newly run experiments. The original MLE, DPO, and IPO comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported MAB reference-logit distribution from normal to uniform; the offline MAB legend changes alpha from 10/sqrt(N) and 1/sqrt(N) to fixed 10 and 1. New LLM experiments introduce four UltraFeedback chunks, DPO initialization followed by three VPO iterations, PairRM feedback, and additional evaluation metrics. Appendix C.2 reports selecting VPO checkpoints across two ranking procedures.

E4.justification: The synthetic alpha-sensitivity comparisons extend to contextual bandits, and the offline MAB regularization comparison is revised. The existing TL;DR exploration-weight ablation and ARC-Challenge analysis of degradation during extended training remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported averaging from 10 to 50 independent runs. Figures 1–2 introduce shaded bands around synthetic results, although their statistical definition is unspecified. No corresponding LLM repeated-run uncertainty or significance testing is added.

E6.justification: v4 adds contextual-bandit outcomes, iterative LLM results in Table 1, and MT-Bench category scores in Figure 5. The best reported VPO LC win rate is 22.53 and MT-Bench mean is 7.62. Revised online MAB curves favor alpha 0.1 over 1.0, reversing v3's ordering under changed settings; this is not a same-setting improvement. ARC-Challenge and TL;DR results are retained.

T1.justification: Assumptions 1–3, Theorems 1–2, token-level derivations, and the proofs in Appendices A–B retain their mathematical substance. Removing stray braces in the indicator expressions around Equations 45–48 is a typesetting correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the unified optimistic/pessimistic VPO framework, reward-calibration contribution, theoretical guarantees, and practical RLHF claims. The additional experiments expand their supporting evidence without redefining these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 newly interprets VPO as competitive with larger models and other iterative alignment methods despite its weaker starting model. Existing explanations of exploration and resistance to over-optimization, and the future-work qualifications about alpha and calibration-policy selection, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds synthetic parameterization, minibatch and beta details; explains the TL;DR calibration buffer; and supplies an ARC prompt example while including the already-tested Llama2-7b model in Appendix C.1. The new iterative setup documents ranking and checkpoint selection, 16 A100 GPUs, and model/dataset access links, although its hyperparameters are largely delegated to a cited work.

R1.justification: v4 adds references covering WIND, reward-biased methods for Markov games, new datasets and evaluators, and DNO/SPPO comparisons. These are localized extensions; the central positioning relative to DPO, reward-biased estimation, and concurrent optimistic/pessimistic methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds a contents section, reorganizes the experimental narrative into separate bandit problems and Buffer/Iterative online setups, expands Appendix C, and makes localized wording corrections. Most introductory, methodological, theoretical, and concluding prose is retained.

P2.justification: The original combined synthetic figure becomes separate online and offline figures with additional contextual-bandit panels, shaded bands, and revised axes and legends. v4 also adds the substantial comparison Table 1 and the MT-Bench radar chart in Appendix C. Existing ARC-Challenge and TL;DR figures are relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The contextual-bandit tests and Zephyr evaluations broaden evidence beyond v3's simpler synthetic problem and PaLM2-based online summarization, while additional runs and implementation details improve transparency. However, Appendix C.2 selects VPO checkpoints across two ranking procedures without reporting equivalent selection for DPO, Table 1's comparative advantages vary by metric and iteration, and the shaded-band statistic is undefined. These limitations keep the net quality gain modest.
